Match the Articles related to the State Legislature:
A. Constitution of Legislatures in States
B. Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
C. Salaries and allowances of members
D. Definition of 'Money Bills'

mcq.s: How many High Courts in India have jurisdiction over more than one State (Union Territories not included)?
mcq.x: Three: the Gauhati High Court (Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh), the Bombay High Court (Maharashtra, Goa) and the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

mcq.s: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India is provided by which Article of the Constitution?
mcq.x: Article 301 (Part XIII) declares that trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India shall be free, subject to the other provisions of Part XIII (Articles 302-307).

mcq.s: Who among the following is NOT an ex-officio (deemed) member of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: The Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
The Chairperson of the Law Commission of India
The Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
The Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
mcq.x: The chairpersons of the national commissions for Minorities, SCs, STs, Women, Backward Classes and Child Rights and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities are deemed members of the NHRC; the Law Commission chairperson is not.

mcq.s: Which Article of the Constitution makes it mandatory to consult the State Public Service Commission on disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the State Government in a civil capacity?
mcq.x: Article 320(3)(c) requires the UPSC or a State PSC to be consulted on all disciplinary matters affecting civil servants of the Union or the State, including memorials and petitions.

mcq.s: In the context of India, which one of the following is the characteristic appropriate for bureaucracy?
o: An agency for widening the scope of parliamentary democracy
An agency for strengthening the structure of federalism
An agency for facilitating political stability and economic growth
An agency for the implementation of public policy
mcq.x: The bureaucracy (permanent executive) carries out the laws and policies made by the political executive and legislature - it is the agency for implementing public policy.

mcq.s: Which of the following is NOT a generally accepted parameter for granting Special Category Status to a State in India?
mcq.x: The Gadgil-formula criteria are hilly terrain, low population density and/or a sizeable tribal population, strategic border location, economic and infrastructural backwardness and non-viable state finances - not a large SC population.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the commencement of the election process in India?
o: The recommendation for election is made by the Government and the notification is issued by the Election Commission
The recommendation for election is made by the Election Commission and the notification is issued by the Home Ministry at the Centre and Home Departments in the States
The recommendation for election is made by the Election Commission and the notification is issued by the President and the Governors of the States concerned
Both the recommendation and the notification are done by the Election Commission
mcq.x: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 the President (Lok Sabha) or the Governor (State Assembly) issues the election notification on the recommendation of the Election Commission.

mcq.s: After the amendment of Rule 27A of the Conduct of Election Rules in March 2024, what is the minimum age for senior citizens to vote from home by postal ballot?
mcq.x: The amendment raised the age for the home postal-ballot facility for senior citizens from 80 to 85 years; it was first used in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

mcq.s:
Match the Constitutional Amendments with their subjects:
A. 13th Amendment
B. 18th Amendment
C. 39th Amendment
D. 52nd Amendment
(i) Nagaland (ii) Anti-defection law (iii) Clarified the term 'State' (iv) Election of the President, Speaker and Prime Minister cannot be challenged in courts
mcq.x: 13th (1962) - special provisions for Nagaland (Art. 371A); 18th (1966) - 'State' in Article 3 includes a Union Territory; 39th (1975) - elections of President, VP, PM and Speaker put beyond courts; 52nd (1985) - anti-defection law.
